title: CI: add snippet sync check to keep docs code blocks aligned with SDK/examples fixtures
author: Sahana Iyer
description:
Context: As part of the streaming/tool-calling/structured-output examples refresh, we’ve repeatedly hit drift between docs-site snippets and the “golden” runnable examples/fixtures. This PR adds a lightweight CI guardrail in the monorepo that fails if (a) a docs snippet references a fixture that doesn’t exist, (b) a fixture referenced by docs has changed but the docs code block wasn’t updated, or (c) the extracted snippet no longer passes basic syntax/lint validation. Goal is copy/paste correctness and reducing regressions during cross-repo updates.

What’s included: 1) A new snippet manifest format and extractor: docs snippets can opt-in by adding a marker line `// rw-snippet: <id>` (or language-appropriate comment) and registering `<id>` in `tools/snippets/snippet_map.yaml`. The check extracts the code fence contents from docs markdown and compares it byte-for-byte (after normalizing line endings + trimming trailing whitespace) with the canonical fixture file. 2) Basic validation per language: Python snippets are parsed with `ast.parse`, TypeScript snippets are typechecked via `tsc --noEmit` using a small tsconfig for snippets, and Go snippets are validated with `go test` in a tiny harness package (no network calls, no API keys). This is intentionally “basic correctness” rather than full execution. 3) A new GitHub Actions job `snippet-sync` wired into required checks for `main`.

Files/areas changed (high level): - tools/snippets/check_snippet_sync.py: extracts code fences, enforces manifest rules, runs validators - tools/snippets/snippet_map.yaml: map of snippet IDs -> fixture paths + language - tools/snippets/validators/{python,ts,go}.py: language-specific validation helpers - .github/workflows/ci.yml: adds `snippet-sync` job (runs on pull_request + merge_group) - docs/: adds/updates a small number of snippet markers for the refreshed pages (no content changes besides markers/normalization) - examples/fixtures/: adds a couple missing fixture files referenced by docs

Notes on conventions: - The check only applies to code fences that opt-in via a snippet marker and a manifest entry; existing docs code blocks without markers are unaffected. - The comparison normalizes CRLF/LF and trims trailing whitespace to avoid platform churn. - For streaming transcripts, we explicitly do NOT validate runtime outputs here; golden transcript stability is covered by ENG-4822 tests in SDK repos.

Why in the monorepo: Docs + examples + quickstarts are touched by multiple teams during this refresh, and we want one central, required gate that catches drift early. This also helps PRs like redwood-docs#512/#519/#527 and redwood-examples#311/#318 stay consistent when changes land out of order.

Test plan: - Verified locally: `python tools/snippets/check_snippet_sync.py --changed-only` and full run `--all` - Simulated drift: edited a docs snippet without updating fixture -> check fails with unified diff - Simulated missing fixture: removed a fixture file -> check fails with actionable error - CI: confirmed new job runs in ~55s on a typical PR and is cached (pip + node + go)

Rollout: - Making `snippet-sync` required for `main` after this merges. - Follow-up: add snippet IDs for the remaining streaming/tool-calling pages once the docs PRs land (tracked in ENG-4821).

Risk: Low. The check is opt-in and should not block unrelated docs changes. If we see false positives, we can temporarily disable per-snippet via manifest while we fix edge cases.

Related: ENG-4821 (audit/parity), ENG-4822 (golden tests); internal docs UI issue INT-3321 (this PR does not address UI, but reduces the churn that made it harder to validate tabs).
commits_summary: tools/snippets: initial snippet manifest + extraction + diff output
validators: add basic python/ts/go validators for snippet code fences
ci: wire snippet-sync job into CI workflow with caching
docs/examples: add snippet markers and fill missing fixture files
review_conversation: Ibrahim Khan: Can we avoid enforcing on every code fence? Some pages have illustrative snippets that aren’t meant to compile. Sahana Iyer: Agreed — this is opt-in only via `rw-snippet` marker + manifest entry. I added a short note in the script error output pointing to the convention. Elliot Price: Diff output is good; can we make the failure actionable for docs writers (i.e., show which file is canonical)? Sahana Iyer: Updated error to print `fixture_path` and a one-liner ‘update docs snippet to match fixture’ vs ‘update fixture and then re-run formatter’. Leila Farouk: The TS validator should not require repo-wide install for small snippets. Can we isolate with a tiny tsconfig and only install deps once? Sahana Iyer: Added `tools/snippets/ts/tsconfig.snippets.json` and reused root `pnpm install` cache; job now uses node_modules cache keyed on lockfile and runs `pnpm -C tools/snippets/ts tsc --noEmit`. Connor O'Brien: Please confirm this won’t break merge queue. Sahana Iyer: Verified `merge_group` trigger and cached dependencies; average runtime under 1 minute. Approved after last change.
release_notes: Internal: Added an opt-in CI check (`snippet-sync`) to prevent drift between docs code snippets and canonical example fixtures; includes basic syntax/type validation for Python/TypeScript/Go.
